chapter_title: Concerning the Three Creations of the Flesh: the ones that were brought forth [...]; and the ones that were begotten by the Abortions; and the ones that were formed of themselves.
chapter_note: After a brief hagiographic dialogue-introduction, the chapter is a continuous, systematic teaching sequence: a threefold classification of earthly life-forms (and their propagation) grounded in Manichaean cosmology (the Ambassador, rulers/powers, and the descent of “thought” as reproductive impulse). No institutional/pastoral or NT overlay appears.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue frame (“Once again…”; “our enlightener… to his disciples”), characteristic of the compiled Kephalaia apparatus rather than the impersonal teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: “All these animals that you see, and also the rest of the [crea]tures [...] of the earth, confirm them in three likeness[es ...]: some from [...] abortions. Others, however, form their own selves in their shape [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic threefold taxonomy of generation (“three likenesses”) describing modes of arising within the cosmic/physical system; no citation, exhortation, or institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: “Also, their nourishment is thre[e ...] light in them, if they shall wish [...]. [...] they eat see[ds and] fr[uit ...]; they eat seeds and fruit. The [...] it entirely, and they [...] the three archetyp[es] from their nature and the [...] the time when they are on the ea[rth ...]; they are seized [...] in their [...]. The Ambassador [...] all powers [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential/technical exposition (nourishment, light-mixture, “three archetypes”) with explicit cosmological agent (The Ambassador) operating within the Manichaean system; still descriptive rather than hortatory.

paragraphs.core_text: “[N] it [...], first [...]. ⟨p.247⟩ Plant them generally to this name: shoots and grass. It formed the bad, bitter trees, the reeds and the thorns and the [...] and these others that are like them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the impersonal classificatory voice: naming categories of vegetation and their formation outcomes (“bad, bitter trees… reeds… thorns”), staying within natural/cosmic mechanics rather than contemporary application.

paragraphs.core_text: “For that thought belongs to the flesh-eating rulers. Still, these [that were] planted (belong to) grass and gourds, since they are in their essence. Nevertheless, [this t]ho[ugh]t that came down from the rulers, as they are in fruit and grass first and shall not be planted in flesh and blood, it formed the trees that shall give nourishing fru[it], as their gourds are sweet.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mechanistic explanation of propagation via descending “thought” associated with rulers; maps cosmological actors → generative principle → plant-types and qualities (sweet/nourishing), without pivot to moral/institutional address.

paragraphs.core_text: “Again, this thou[ght] that came down from the powers that eat m[ea]t and also eat grass and gourds, it has formed the trees that shall not produce any nourishment. Their fruits belong neither to good nor evil.”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closes the schema by iterating the same causal mechanism (“thought… came down”) to account for another botanical class; the balanced valuation (“neither to good nor evil”) remains within descriptive cosmological-natural classification.
